prompt:

Asset type: one coherent 3:2 interior concept for a cozy seaside grocery game.

Image2 is a FURNITURE DESIGN and FOOTPRINT reference only: two fitted turquoise/oak display cabinets, shortened left run leaving doorway clear, cashier counter in foreground right. The input perspective errors must NOT be preserved.
REDRAW THE WHOLE ROOM AND FURNITURE with a single mathematically consistent ORTHOGRAPHIC DIMETRIC 3D camera. This is an architectural visualization rendered in polished casual-game materials. No perspective vanishing convergence, no independently rotated furniture sprites.
EXACT PROJECTED ROOM AXES:
Every long edge belonging to the LEFT wall axis runs up to the right at 25 degrees on the image. Every long edge belonging to the RIGHT wall axis runs down to the right at 20 degrees on the image. All vertical edges are vertical.
Use these same TWO constant directions for EVERYTHING: ceiling beams, horizontal window-frame edges, window sill, wall skirting, furniture backs, top rails, every long shelf lip, tray edges, lower storage-bay rails, cabinet plinths, counter front AND back edges, countertop and counter base. These are projected axes of a true rectangular 90-degree room in an orthographic view.
The BACK plane of the left cabinet is exactly FLUSH with the left wall. The BACK plane of the right cabinet is exactly FLUSH with the right wall. They meet as an L-shaped fitted cabinet installation in the rear corner. The visible rear corner remains about the center of the canvas. Both units have the same height, shallow depth, shelf design, trim and raised base; the LEFT run is SHORTER because the door needs clearance. No wedge-shaped furniture-wall gaps, no angled cabinets, no furniture standing diagonally away from its wall. Every cabinet foot touches the floor.
CRITICAL ENTRANCE CLEARANCE:
Preserve a fully visible wide open door at far left with its inner jamb near x18% of the image. The entire LEFT cabinet, including front protrusions and plinth, begins at x28% or farther right. It only occupies the FARTHER section of the window wall near the rear corner. The closest section under the window is bare wall. Keep a broad clear floor corridor from the threshold into the center, at least one comfortable person's width, approximately 90cm. No furniture overlaps the doorway, threshold, swing or floor approach. Do not move/narrow the doorway to fake clearance.

Honey-oak wood, turquoise paneled base and curved turquoise side supports with cream edge trim, two generous open display tiers above lower wicker storage. Low shallow wicker product trays with ONLY TWO weave rows on their front rim. Upper tier has a few spaced milk bottles, honey/jam jars and lemons; middle has a pear and loaf in shallow trays. Goods are readable, consistent size, grounded on shelves. Matching design, not forced identical screen length. Elegant compact cabinetry hugging both walls, not bulky freestanding blocks.
CASHIER COUNTER:
Place one broad honey-oak/turquoise/cream cashier counter with antique brass register in foreground RIGHT, preserving a clear working aisle behind it and an open central approach on its left. Its long front countertop edge, back countertop edge, front base/plinth edge and rear base edge MUST ALL run down-right at EXACTLY the same 20-degree projected direction as the RIGHT wall skirting and RIGHT display shelf edges. Its short depth edges MUST ALL run up-right at the SAME25-degree projected direction as the LEFT wall. All front columns vertical. It is axis-aligned with the room, not casually turned toward the viewer. Both top and base are rectangular boxes in one shared orthographic space. No independent 30-degree counter rotation.
Compose a believable beautiful working shop with abundant but organized cabinet area; preserve free doorway/aisles. Warm golden directional sunlight from the left, soft contact shadows, cream plaster, rich turquoise trim, tactile oak grain and wicker, sparkling Mediterranean sea beyond window and door. High-detail cozy dimensional raster game art. Redraw architectural projection as needed to enforce the common axes; keep the same recognizable room identity and broad framing. No signs, lettering, arrows, measurements, diagram overlays, interface, people, extra furniture, watermark or border.
